title: What inflation does to a fixed amount of money
label: Clearly identified as an education edition, never as news.
facts: No statistics; arithmetic illustrations only, with assumptions stated.

captions.facebook:
FINANCIAL EDUCATION · Education edition

What inflation does to a fixed amount of money

Illustration: if prices rise 3% a year, $100 buys about $97 of today's shopping after one year and about $74 after ten.

That 3% is an assumption for the arithmetic, not a forecast.

Money that sits still does not lose its number, but it can lose what it buys.

Understanding this helps households read their pay rises, savings and price changes in real terms.

Learn. Understand. Stay Informed.
